sections.title: BIC consequences and the limits of discarded terms

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayes-factor-computation-C004 (partial): The success condition requires the entry's hypotheses to be supplied, and the failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. The lemma thm:p15-laplace-curvature-replacement (body 122-138) states only these hypotheses: F_n=nJ_n with J_n symmetric and eigenvalues >= c, ||J~_n-J_n|| <= delta_n < c/2, and the mode, likelihood and prior ordinate held fixed. Those hypotheses support only the bound |log Î(F~_n)/Î(F_n)| <= d delta_n/c. The entry also concludes that 'delta_n=O(n^-1/2) gives relative error O(n^-1/2)', that 'O(n^-1) preserves that smaller error order', and that expected information may be substituted. These are relative errors against I_n, so they need Î(F_n)/I_n=1+O(n^-1), which holds only under the MLE Laplace hypotheses of thm:p15-laplace-mode-variants / def:p15-laplace-family. The lemma never states those hypotheses. The annex proof ends (lines 106-109) by 'multiplication by the already proved 1+O(n^-1) approximation', which is proved only under them. The companion boundary theorem has to verify them separately (annex 391-393).

ED26-P15-CH-bayes-factor-computation-C005 (partial): The statement (body 430-459) is present and its annex proof (113-132) is written out. The worked boundaries are also present: the BIC-to-exact ratio tends to 2, and the unit-information instance works. The element 'preserve the identified source variants' is not met, and the failure condition 'unsupported source attribution' holds at the component's Sec. 4.1.3 locator. (a) Body 471-473 attributes 'Different blockwise information rates, singular curvature, boundary modes and increasing dimension require other results' to \cite[Sec.~4.1.3]. The held source's Sec. 4.1.3 (pp. 778-779) covers only n as the Hessian growth rate and two-stage hierarchical models. Boundary modes are in Sec. 4.1.2 (Hsiao 1994, p. 778), large degrees of freedom are in Sec. 4.4 (p. 781), and singular curvature appears nowhere in Sec. 4. (b) The 'before discarding terms' display and the remark that 'both prior-log terms have coefficient two' (body 461-469) differ from the source's printed eq. (6) (p. 778), which gives those terms coefficient one. The text never identifies the printed variant, although it does flag the printed eq. (12) explicitly at body 647-651. (c) Two source variants at this locator are not presented. The source states (9), (S - log B12)/log B12 -> 0, without any condition; the handbook gives it only as its own conditional clause, with no attribution. Jeffreys's S + c with a Cauchy-prior constant (p. 779; the source calls it 'Jeffreys's variant' of the Schwarz criterion on p. 781) does not appear anywhere in the chapter.
